newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP Griffin oil output seen resuming.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP Griffin oil output seen resuming.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) would probably resume production from its Griffin oil field offshore Western Australia this evening, a company official told Reuters on Friday.
Production was halted on Thursday because of a tropical depression.
It now appeared that the depression would not develop into a tropical cyclone but a watching brief would be maintained, the BHP official said.
"At the moment, if it does not form into a cyclone, we'll probably go back into production later this evening," he said.
Production was expected to resume at normal levels, he said.
BHP holds a 45 percent stake in the 80,000 barrels per day Griffin field, Mobil Corp 35 percent and Inpex Alpha Ltd 20 percent.
The two fields are off western Australia.
The tropical depression was at present producing 20-30 knot winds and some fairly heavy rain. "That's no trouble for us," the BHP official said.
A spokesman for Woodside Petroleum Ltd was not immediately available to comment on whether the Cossack oil field, nearby BHP's Griffin field, was about to be brought back into production.
